title: Add role definitions, a steward role, and a requirements ladder
summary: Add recorded role definitions and a first steward role that runs in parallel every 5 finished tasks. It reads Athena's state in place and queues work items, including one for each blind spot. A requirements ladder (owner goals, brief requirements, design decisions, defaults and conventions, implementation) lets it change only the lower rungs itself and propose the upper ones with evidence.

defaults_applied.how: All new code is Rust in the existing crates.
New modules ship with tests; cargo test and clippy pass.
Start with one role and one ladder; no other roles.
The design note and changelog are written for an outside reader.
Details recovered from BRIEF.md and the requirements map, with the user's reply fixing the ladder.
The ladder is enforced by a function with tests, not prose.
Behavior is checked through cargo test with the fake agent.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Cadence counts finished tasks (landed or rejected) since the steward's last run, kept as a persisted counter.
The steward writes proposals and work items only; it does not edit the owner's goals or BRIEF.md.
Data it cannot read (for example records/ or history absent from its view) becomes a blind-spot work item.

Rungs from design decisions down are the ones the steward may change itself, but this first version only applies changes on the lowest two (defaults/conventions, implementation); upper rungs are proposed with evidence.
Athena's checks and the independent verifier still gate any change the steward applies.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena-data has a role definition record (name, goal, prompt, cadence in finished tasks, highest rung it may change itself) and one steward definition with a short stable prompt.

A work item record names its source by reference (job id, path or commit) and carries evidence by reference, not copied data. It has a field for the requirement rung it concerns, and a kind for a blind spot.

A Ladder enum in athena-data orders five rungs: OwnerGoals, BriefRequirements, DesignDecisions, DefaultsConventions, Implementation. A function decides whether a role may change a rung itself (only DesignDecisions and below, or whatever the role's limit is, never the top two) or must queue a proposal.
Run cargo test: with the fake agent, finishing the 5th task starts the steward without blocking the main flow, and the 4th does not.
Run cargo test: when a data source is unreadable, the steward queues a work item that names the blind spot and its source.
Run cargo test: a proposed change on a rung above the role's limit is queued with evidence and not applied. A change on a lower rung is applied.
Run cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check, then cargo test: all clean and passing.
docs/design/requirements-map.md moves A9-1 and A10-1 to covered, naming the code. CHANGELOG.md has an entry. A short design note gives the alternatives and the ladder.

out_of_scope: Role cost and yield tracking, reshaping and retirement (rest of A10-1 and A9-2)
Changing owner goals, brief requirements or athena.toml
Copying Athena's state into new records
departures: This touches several crates and needs scheduler wiring plus design docs, so cost and time are above the reference, and p_verification_passes is lower.
